0x10001900.comment:
Safely deletes a dynamically allocated object using the C++ delete operator.

0x10001960.name: InitializeCelContextInfo
strings: 0x27D94|s_[sGetCelContextInfo]_This_should_10027d94|[sGetCelContextInfo] This should not happen. Please tell Jon Morin!
0x10001960.comment:
Initialize cel context information for D2 graphics rendering

Algorithm:
1. Extract component index from unit structure at offset +0x1d
2. Copy unit type, unit ID, and class ID from source unit to cel context
3. Lookup component type from global table using component index
4. Lookup weapon class from global table using unit class ID  
5. Lookup unit type info from global table using unit type
6. Set default cel file name to 'lit ' (0x2074696c)
7. Check for custom cel file override in unit component array
8. Validate COF data pointer exists in unit structure at +0xb8
9. Call FUN_10001c20 to get COF data with dimensions and cel file info
10. Loop through COF component entries to find matching component
11. Check component index bounds (must be < 16, validate with 0xf)
12. When matching component found, set animation direction flags
13. Extract 4-byte cel file name from COF component data
14. Replace null bytes in cel file name with space (0x20) for padding
15. Validate all required context fields are non-zero before return
16. Set default values for missing cel file and component flags

Parameters:
pUnit (int*): Pointer to unit structure containing type, ID, class, and component data
pCelContext (int*): Output cel context structure to populate with rendering info

Returns:
void: Function terminates with FUN_100149f1(-1) on validation failures

Special Cases:
- Animation direction: Set to 0 if unit type < 5, otherwise set to 1
- Missing cel file override: Uses default 'lit ' name (0x2074696c)
- Null bytes in cel file: Replaced with space character (0x20)
- Missing component/weapon class: Set to default 'xxx ' (0x20787878)
- Validation failures: Call error logging then terminate process

Magic Numbers:
0x1d - Component index offset in unit structure
0x24, 0x28 - Unit type and ID offsets in cel context  
0x34, 0x38, 0x3c, 0x40 - Component info offsets in cel context
0xb8 - COF data pointer offset in unit structure
0x2074696c - Default 'lit ' cel file name
0x20787878 - Default 'xxx ' component name  
0xf - Maximum component index (16 components: 0-15)
0x5 - Animation direction threshold for unit types

Structure Layout:
Unit Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type  | Description
+0x1c  | 4    | dwUnitType   | uint  | Unit type identifier
+0x1d  | 1    | bComponent   | byte  | Component index for this unit
+0x20  | 4    | dwUnitId     | uint  | Unique unit identifier
+0x24  | 4    | dwClassId    | uint  | Unit class/subtype
+0x38  | 64   | celOverrides | uint[16] | Custom cel file overrides by component
+0xb8  | 4    | pCofData     | void* | Pointer to COF animation data

Cel Context Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name        | Type  | Description  
+0x1d  | 1    | bComponent       | byte  | Component index
+0x20  | 4    | dwFlags          | uint  | Animation direction flags
+0x24  | 4    | dwUnitType      | uint  | Unit type identifier
+0x28  | 4    | dwUnitId        | uint  | Unique unit identifier  
+0x30  | 4    | dwUnitToType    | uint  | Unit type lookup value
+0x34  | 4    | dwComponentType | uint  | Component type from table
+0x38  | 4    | dwCelFile       | uint  | 4-char cel file name
+0x3c  | 4    | dwWClass        | uint  | Weapon class identifier
+0x40  | 4    | dwComponentFlags| uint  | Component-specific flags

0x10002050.name: ProcessCompositeUnitGraphics
0x10002050.comment:
Processes and renders composite unit graphics components.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input composite unit pointer for null
2. Check unit visibility flags using gdwBitMasks_exref bitmasks
3. Extract base width (field 5) and height (field 6) from composite unit
4. Validate graphics info pointer at offset 0x2e exists
5. Iterate through graphics info linked list to find matching frame
6. Match by animation type (field 8) and direction lookup (field 9)
7. Validate COF (Component Object File) data pointer exists
8. Extract frame position from unit coordinates (field 1 & 2)
9. Calculate frame data offset using COF header and position
10. First pass: count valid components and calculate maximum width
11. For each component in COF data validate component type < 16
12. Initialize component structure with unit reference and coordinates
13. Call thunk_FUN_10001960 to set up component rendering context
14. Call Ordinal_10055 to prepare component for rendering
15. Call Ordinal_10040 to get component width and update maximum
16. Second pass: render all components if count > 0
17. For each component call Ordinal_10079 to perform actual rendering

Parameters:
pCompositeUnit (uint*): Pointer to composite unit structure containing:
  Field 0: Visibility flags
  Field 1: X coordinate (byte)
  Field 2: Y coordinate with direction in upper bits
  Field 5: Base width
  Field 6: Base height 
  Field 8: Animation type identifier
  Field 9: Direction index for lookup table
  Field 0x2e: Pointer to graphics info linked list

Returns:
void - No return value, performs rendering side effects

Special Cases:
- Null pointer validation with assertion and exit(-1)
- Missing graphics info assertion and exit(-1)
- Missing COF data assertion and exit(-1)
- Component type >= 16 assertion and exit(-1)
- Empty COF (no components) returns immediately
- Zero valid components returns without rendering

Error Handling:
All error conditions trigger Ordinal_10021 assertion with source file and line
followed by FUN_100149f1(0xffffffff) which exits the process

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x44e - Line number for null unit pointer check
0x45e - Line number for null graphics info check  
0x466 - Line number for null COF data check
0x2ad - Line number for null frame data check
0x429 - Line number for invalid component type check
0x475 - Line number for component type check in render loop
0x2e - Offset to graphics info pointer in composite unit
0x14 - Offset to COF data in graphics info node
0x1c - COF header size before component data

0x100052C0.comment:
Allocates and initializes a unit object with specified attributes.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x58 (88) bytes of memory for unit structure
2. Clear all fields to zero
3. Set type field (offset 0) to 0xc
4. Apply type and state bit masks to field at offset 2
5. Store parameters into structure fields (type, subtype, coordinates, gfx type)
6. Set function pointers for event handlers
7. Copy initialization data from pdwInitData or use defaults
8. Invoke post-initialization handler (FUN_6f90ea50)
9. Return allocated unit pointer

Parameters:
- nUnitType (ECX): Unit type identifier (stored at offset 0xc)
- nSubType (EDX): Unit subtype/class (stored at offset 0x14)
- nX (Stack+0x4): X coordinate (stored at offset 0x18)
- nY (Stack+0x8): Y coordinate (stored at offset 0x1c)
- nGfxType (Stack+0xc): Graphics type flag (stored at offset 0x4c)
- pdwInitData (Stack+0x10): Optional pointer to 2-dword initialization data

Returns:
- void*: Pointer to newly allocated and initialized unit structure

0x10005640.comment:

3. Calculate string length using strlen-like loop

5. Copy remaining bytes individually
6. Return 1 on success, 0 if source is NULL

- pszDest (byte *): Destination buffer to receive string copy

Returns:
- 1 if copy succeeded
- 0 if source string was NULL

Allocates and initializes a game object structure (96 bytes).

1. Allocate 96-byte block via FogMemAlloc
2. Zero-initialize all fields via loop
3. Set base flags in fields [0] and [2] with bitmask values
4. Populate object fields from parameters

- dwValue5 (uint): Field [1] value
- dwValue6 (uint): Field [0x11] value

0x10005B30.comment:

2. Reads current state from field 0x14

0x10005BB0.name: ValidateCelBounds
0x10005BB0.comment:
Validates whether a Cel sprite fits within screen boundaries.

Algorithm:
1. Verify pCelInfo parameter type is 2
2. Extract table index from pCelInfo[0x10] and pCelInfo[0x14]
3. Load CelFileInfo for the cel (width, height, mode, etc.)
4. Check bounds: cel must fit within screen with margins
5. Return 1 if valid, 0 if out of bounds

Parameters:
- pCelInfo (int *): Cel information structure, pCelInfo[0] must equal 2

Returns:
- 1 if cel fits within screen bounds
- 0 if cel exceeds screen boundaries

Magic Numbers:
- 0x10, 0x14: Offsets into pCelInfo structure
- 0x73: Line number in FogAssert
- 0xffffffff: Error code for assertion failure

0x10005CD0.name: RenderAnimatedGameObject
0x10005CD0.comment:
Renders an animated game object by managing animation state, frame timing, and cel drawing.

Classification: Worker function (render callback for type 2 game objects)

Algorithm:
1. Validate object type == 2, assert failure if not
2. Zero-initialize 0x12 dwords of local CelFileInfo array
3. Early exit with success (1) if no cel data (field[1]) and no anim table (field[0x10])
4. Cache position from fields[3] (X) and [4] (Y)
5. If animation table exists (field[0x10] != 0):
   a. Get animation mode from field[0x14]
   b. If mode is 0 or 1, validate cel bounds and update mode
   c. If mode changed, invoke optional callback at field[0x16]
   d. Get frame count from current animation entry
   e. Handle animation state transitions:
      - State 2: If at end, reset to frame 0 and transition to state 3
      - State 4: If at end, reset to frame 0 and transition to state 1
   f. Reset timestamp via GetTickCount on state transition
   g. Clamp frame index to valid range
6. Load cel pointers:
   a. If no anim table: use field[1] as single cel, adjust position by cel dimensions
   b. If anim table: index by (field[0x10] + field[0x14] * 0x10) for primary/secondary cels
7. Render primary cel via GfxInterfaceCall84 if present
8. Render secondary cel via GfxInterfaceCall84 if present
9. Update frame animation based on elapsed time:
   a. Calculate frame duration: (direction * 1000) / 25 ms per frame
   b. For states 2/4: linear frame progression clamped to max
   c. For other states: looping frame calculation via modulo

Parameters:
- pAnimObject (int * via ECX): Pointer to 96-byte game object structure

Returns:
- 1: Always returns success

Offset  Size  Field              Description
0x00    4     dwType             Type identifier (must be 2)
0x01    4     pCelFile           Single cel file pointer (when no anim table)
0x03    4     dwPosX             X coordinate
0x04    4     dwPosY             Y coordinate
0x10    4     pAnimTable         Animation table base pointer
0x11    4     nDirection         Animation direction value
0x12    4     dwStartTick        Animation start timestamp
0x13    4     nCurrentFrame      Current frame index
0x14    4     nAnimState         Animation state (0-4)
0x15    4     dwPrimaryAlpha     Primary cel alpha value
0x16    4     pfnStateCallback   Optional state change callback
0x17    4     fAnimEnabled       Animation enabled flag

Animation Table Entry (16 bytes per state):
Offset  Size  Field              Description
0x00    4     ppCelPrimary       Pointer to primary cel pointer
0x04    4     ppCelSecondary     Pointer to secondary cel pointer
0x08    4     dwAlpha            Secondary cel alpha
0x0C    4     nDirection         Direction for this state

0 = Initial/Idle
1 = Active (looping)
2 = Playing forward (clamps at end, transitions to 3)
3 = Stopped at end
4 = Playing forward (clamps at end, transitions to 1)

0x10006080.name: AnimCallbackUpdateState
0x10006080.comment:
AnimCallbackUpdateState - Invokes animation update callback and manages state transitions.

Algorithm:
1. Dereference ppAnimHandle to get pAnimObj (D2WIN_IMAGE structure)
2. Assert pAnimObj->eType == 2 (D2WIN_IMAGE type validation)
3. Check if pAnimObj->pfnUpdateCallback (offset 0x34) is non-null
4. If null, return 0 (no callback to invoke)
5. Call pfnUpdateCallback(ppAnimHandle) and capture return value
6. If callback returns 0, return 0 (no state change needed)
7. Check current state at pAnimObj->nState (offset 0x50):
   - If state == 3: transition to state 4
   - If state == 1: transition to state 2
   - Otherwise: return callback result unchanged
8. Clear pAnimObj->nFrameCounter (offset 0x4C) to 0
9. Store GetTickCount() in pAnimObj->dwLastTick (offset 0x48)
10. Return callback result

Parameters:
- ppAnimHandle (int**): Double pointer to animation object handle

Returns:
- int: Result from pfnUpdateCallback, or 0 if no callback

State Transitions:
- State 1 -> 2: Animation starting -> playing
- State 3 -> 4: Animation stopping -> stopped

Offset  Size  Field              Type        Description
0x00    4     eType              uint        Type marker (must be 2)
0x34    4     pfnUpdateCallback  code*       Update callback function pointer
0x48    4     dwLastTick         DWORD       Last update tick count
0x4C    4     nFrameCounter      int         Frame counter (reset on transition)
0x50    4     nState             int         Animation state (1-4)

0x1000B670.name: SearchGlyphDataBinary
0x1000B670.comment:
Binary search for character glyph data in East Asian font tables.

Used as g_pfnValueProcessor callback for East Asian locales (Chinese, Japanese,
Korean) and font ID 0xd. Unlike GetCharacterGlyphData which uses direct array
indexing for ASCII fonts, this performs binary search through sorted Unicode
glyph tables containing thousands of entries.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize search bounds: low=0, high=(glyph count - 1)
2. Loop with iteration limit (max 1001 iterations for safety)
3. Calculate mid index, compare character codes
4. If match found, return pointer to glyph entry
5. Adjust bounds: if target < mid, search lower half; else upper half
6. If not found, return pointer to default glyph at offset 0x1b2 (entry 31)

Parameters:
- wCharCode (ushort via CX): Unicode character code to look up

Returns:
- int *: Pointer to 14-byte glyph data entry in font table
         Returns default glyph (offset 0x1b2) if not found

Magic Numbers:
- 0x14 (20): Font cache entry stride (5 DWORDs per font slot)
- 0xe (14): Glyph entry size in bytes
- 0x3e9 (1001): Maximum search iterations (safety limit)
- 0x1b2 (434): Offset to default/fallback glyph entry (31 * 14)
- +8: Offset to glyph count field in font header

Globals Referenced:
- g_nCurrentFontIndex: Currently active font slot index
- g_pFontHandles: Font header pointers array (glyph count at +8)
- g_pFontDataPtrs: Font glyph data pointers array

Related Functions:

0x1000B730.name: MeasureTextWidthWithEscapes

1. Initialize sum (nSum) and index (nIdx) to 0
2. Return 0 immediately if input array pointer is null
3. Set position counter (nPos) to 3
4. Loop through array until null terminator:
   - Return accumulated sum if current index exceeds nLimit
   - If value equals 0x0A (newline), skip and advance all counters
   - Otherwise validate: value must be 0xFF followed by two digits (0x30-0x36)
   - If validation fails, call g_pfnValueProcessor and add byte at offset +3 to sum
   - Advance array pointer, index, and position counters appropriately
5. Return accumulated sum

Parameters:
- pData (ushort*): Pointer to null-terminated ushort array to process
- nLimit (int): Maximum index/position limit for array traversal

Returns:

5. Callback returns character-specific width info at offset +3
6. Accumulate all non-newline character widths into nTotalWidth
7. Advance to next character in array, increment loop counter
8. Return accumulated nTotalWidth sum

- nMaxLength (int): Maximum number of characters to process

0x1000D6C0.name: ProcessType2UIElementClick
0x1000D6C0.comment:

   a. Check Y bounds: regionY <= (g_nScreenHeight - elementY) < (regionY + regionHeight)
   b. Check X bounds: (regionX - regionWidth) <= adjustedX < regionX
   c. If hit, call region handler at piSubRegions[regionIndex * 5 + 4](pUIElement)
   d. Advance by 5 dwords per region, check next entry flag at offset +9
8. If no sub-region matched and default handler exists at offset [0xd]:
   a. Call default handler: element[0xd](pUIElement)
9. Return handler result or 0 if no handler invoked

Parameters:
- pUIElement (Stack+4): Pointer to UI element structure

Returns:

Offset  Size  Field           Description
0x00    4     eType           Element type (must be 2)
0x04    4     dwFlags         Flags combined with gdwBitMasks
0x08    4     dwMaskBits      Visibility mask bits
0x0c    4     nY              Y coordinate
0x10    4     nX              X coordinate
0x14    4     nWidth          Width
0x18    4     nHeight         Height
0x34    4     pfnCallback     Default click handler function pointer
0x48    4     pSubRegions     Pointer to sub-region table

Sub-Region Entry (20 bytes / 5 dwords):
Offset  Size  Field           Description
0x00    4     nY              Region Y position
0x04    4     nX              Region X position
0x08    4     nHeight         Region height
0x0c    4     nWidth          Region width
0x10    4     pfnHandler      Region click handler

6. Store cursor position to g_nScreenHeight/g_nScreenWidth globals
7. Check if screen popup is active via IsScreenPopupActiveBitSet
8. If popup active, invoke screen handler and process inventory, return if handled
9. Get control list from g_dwLastInventoryItem or g_pInventoryList
10. Switch on message type (pMouseMsg[1]):
    - 0x201 (WM_LBUTTONDOWN) / 0x204 (WM_RBUTTONDOWN): Set g_dwGameState=1, iterate controls for hit-test and invoke button-down callback at offset +0x24
    - 0x202 (WM_LBUTTONUP) / 0x205 (WM_RBUTTONUP): Set g_dwGameState=0, iterate controls and invoke button-up callback at offset +0x28
11. Insert message cookie into cache via InsertCacheNodeWithCookie

Parameters:
  pMouseMsg - Pointer to mouse message structure:
    +0x00: Control pointer (set by handler)
    +0x04: Message type (0x201-0x205)
    +0x0C: LPARAM containing X/Y coordinates

Returns: void

Control Structure Offsets (UI Element):
  +0x0C: nLeft (int) - Left boundary X coordinate
  +0x10: nRight (int) - Right boundary X coordinate  
  +0x14: nHeight (int) - Height of control
  +0x18: nOffsetX (int) - Horizontal offset adjustment
  +0x24: pfnOnMouseDown (code*) - Mouse down callback handler
  +0x28: pfnOnMouseUp (code*) - Mouse up callback handler
  +0x38: pfnHitTest (code*) - Custom hit-test callback (NULL for default bounds check)
  +0x3C: pNextControl (ptr) - Next control in linked list

Magic Numbers:
  0x201 = WM_LBUTTONDOWN - Left mouse button pressed
  0x202 = WM_LBUTTONUP - Left mouse button released
  0x204 = WM_RBUTTONDOWN - Right mouse button pressed
  0x205 = WM_RBUTTONUP - Right mouse button released

Globals Modified:
  g_nScreenHeight - Current cursor Y position
  g_nScreenWidth - Current cursor X position
  g_dwGameState - Mouse button state (1=down, 0=up)
  g_nCallbackDepth - Callback nesting depth counter

Decompiler Variable Mapping (cannot rename due to boundary issue):
  dwCookieValue -> pMouseMsg (saved parameter)
  iVar1 -> nHandlerResult / pCurrentControl
  iVar2 -> nCallbackResult
  dVar3 -> nCursorX
  uVar4 -> wMouseX (extracted X from LPARAM)
  uVar5 -> wMouseY (extracted Y from LPARAM)
  dVar6 -> nCursorY
  dStack_4 -> nAdjustedY

0x10010A00.name: ProcessPaletteCleanup
0x10010A00.comment:
Manages periodic palette data cleanup with timer-based rate limiting.

Algorithm:
1. Check if cleanup is active (g_dwCleanupActive)
2. If inactive, exit immediately
3. If active but timer not enabled, disable cleanup
4. If timer enabled, check elapsed time since last update
5. If less than 2001ms (0x7d1) elapsed, exit to throttle calls
6. Update last tick count and decrement countdown counter
7. When countdown reaches 0, reset cleanup flags and call cleanup handler

Parameters:

- IMPLICIT: g_dwTimerEnabled: Timer enabled flag  
- IMPLICIT: g_dwLastTickCount: Last recorded tick count
- IMPLICIT: g_dwCountdown: Remaining cleanup iterations

Returns:
- void

Magic Numbers:
- 0x7d0 (2000): Minimum milliseconds between cleanup calls
- GetTickCount(): System timer for rate limiting

3. If disabled: disable timer and cleanup flags
4. Call palette cleanup handler in both cases

Parameters:

Returns:

2. Allocate new structure (0x468 bytes) via FogMemAlloc
3. Zero-fill entire structure using REP STOSD (282 dwords)
4. Set object type field to 0xB
5. Configure bit flags from gdwBitMasks_exref (3 flag sources)
6. Store screen dimensions from globals g_nScreenHeight, g_nScreenWidth
7. Install function pointers for event handlers at offsets [7] and [8]
8. Initialize remaining fields to 0
9. Link object to global list via LinkObjectToList
10. Store reference in g_pCurrentScreenData

Parameters:

- IMPLICIT: Uses global variables g_nScreenHeight, g_nScreenWidth, gdwBitMasks_exref

Returns:
- void (result stored in global g_pCurrentScreenData)

Magic Numbers:
- 0x468 (1128): Structure size in bytes
- 0x11A (282): Number of dwords to zero-fill
- 0xB: Screen object type constant
- Offsets [2-0xD]: Structure field indices storing flags and dimensions

4. Return 1 if both bits set, 0 otherwise

- 0 otherwise

0x10010E00.name: ValidateCharacterData

Validates and registers a character in the current screen data.

1. Verify current screen is popup type (0xb), assert if not
2. Check if character count (at offset 0x10) exceeds 7, return 0 if true
3. Copy character data (33 dwords) to screen data at calculated offset
4. Call Ordinal_10127 to trigger character redraw update
5. Calculate character value via SumCharacterValues
6. Update max value field, increment character count, update display stride

0x10010EC0.name: TryInvokeScreenHandler

2. Check if both bit flags in gdwBitMasks are set on g_pCurrentScreenData[2]
3. Verify screen has a valid handler index (g_pCurrentScreenData[0x119] != -1)
4. Calculate handler function pointer from screen data using stride 0x21 (33) bytes
5. If pointer is non-null, invoke it and return 1, otherwise return 0

Parameters:
- None

Returns:
- 1 if handler was invoked
- 0 if conditions not met or handler pointer is null

0x10010F50.name: CalculatePopupHoverColumn
0x10010F50.comment:
Calculates which column the mouse is hovering over in a popup window.
Called as a callback from the screen object event system.

Algorithm:
1. Validate object type is 0xB (D2WIN_POPUP)
2. Check visibility flags via gdwBitMasks_exref (offset +8 AND offset +0)
3. If not visible/interactive, return 0 (not handled)
4. Initialize selected column to -1 at offset 0x464
5. Calculate relative X position from popup bounds
6. Validate mouse Y is within popup height bounds
7. Validate mouse X is within popup width bounds
8. If within bounds, calculate column index: X / 20 pixels

Parameters:
- pPopupData (ECX): Pointer to popup structure (type 0xB)
  - [0x00] eType: Object type, must be 0xB
  - [0x08] dwFlags: Visibility/interaction flags
  - [0x0C] nY: Top Y coordinate
  - [0x10] nWidth: Popup width
  - [0x14] nHeight: Popup height
  - [0x18] nRight: Right X coordinate
  - [0x464] nSelectedColumn: Output hover column index

Returns:
- 1: Mouse within popup bounds (column calculated)
- 0: Mouse outside bounds or popup not visible

Magic Numbers:
- 0xB: D2WIN_POPUP object type constant
- 0x14 (20): Column width in pixels
- 0x119 (281): DWORD index for selected column field (offset 0x464)
- -1 (0xFFFFFFFF): Invalid/no column selected

0x10011020.name: RenderPopupContent
0x10011020.comment:
Renders popup menu content with multiple text lines and selection highlighting.
Called as a callback from the screen object event system at offset 0x1C.

NOTE: Function boundary is broken (single instruction detected). Variable types and
names documented here but cannot be applied via MCP tools until boundary is fixed.

Algorithm:
1. Validate object type is 0xB (D2WIN_POPUP) via FogAssert
2. Check visibility flags in gdwBitMasks (bits at offset +0 and +8)
3. If not visible, return 0 (not handled)
4. Find palette index for gray color (0x3F, 0x3F, 0x3F) for background
5. Calculate background rectangle bounds from popup dimensions with 5px padding
6. Draw semi-transparent background via Ordinal_10052 (D2Gfx.DrawFilledRect)
7. Validate clip coordinates via GfxValidateClipCoordinates
8. Set active font to index 1
9. Loop through all text lines (count at offset 0x40):
   a. Get text pointer from popup+0x44 (0x84 bytes per line)
   b. Calculate Y position: baseY + ((lineIndex - lineCount) + 1) * 0x14
   c. Determine text color: 3 if selected (matches offset 0x464), 0 otherwise
   d. Call RenderUnicodeTextWithLineHeight for each line
10. Return 1 (handled)

Parameters:
- pPopupData (ECX): Pointer to popup structure (type 0xB)
  [0x00] eType: Object type constant 0xB
  [0x08] dwFlags: Visibility/interaction flags
  [0x0C] nY: Top Y coordinate
  [0x10] nX: Left X coordinate
  [0x14] nHeight: Popup height
  [0x18] nWidth: Popup width
  [0x40] nLineCount: Number of text lines
  [0x44] szLines[]: Unicode text lines (0x84 bytes each = 66 wchar_t)
  [0x464] nSelectedLine: Currently highlighted line index (-1 if none)

Returns:
- 1: Popup was visible and rendered
- 0: Popup not visible (flags not set)

Magic Numbers:
- 0xB: D2WIN_POPUP object type constant
- 0x14 (20): Line height in pixels
- 0x84 (132): Bytes per text line (66 wchar_t)
- 0x3F: Gray color component (63/255)
- 0xFF: Alpha value for background rectangle
- 5: Padding pixels around popup content

Ordinal Calls:
- Ordinal_10052: D2Gfx.DrawFilledRect - Draws filled rectangle with alpha

Variable Mapping (cannot rename due to broken boundary):
- uVar1 -> byPaletteIndex (byte): Palette index for gray background color
- iVar2 -> nLineCount (int): Number of text lines from offset 0x40
- iVar3 -> nLineIndex (int): Loop counter for rendering text lines
- pszText -> pwszLineText (Unicode*): Pointer to current Unicode text line
- unaff_ESI, unaff_EBX: Phantom registers from decompiler (ignore)
- iStack_10..iStack_4: Background rectangle coordinates (nTop, nBottom, nLeft, nRight)

0x100112D0.name: RenderProgressBar
0x100112D0.comment:
Renders a progress bar UI element by drawing a colored rectangle.

Classification: Callback/Handler - render callback for D2WIN_PROGRESSBAR type (eType=10)

Algorithm:
1. Validate pProgressBarData->eType == D2WIN_PROGRESSBAR (10), assert if invalid
2. Check visibility flags at offset 0x8 against gdwBitMasks_exref[0] and gdwBitMasks_exref[2]
3. If not visible, return 0 (nothing drawn)
4. Find red color palette index via FindPaletteIndexForColor(0xff, 0, 0)
5. Extract coordinates from progress bar structure:
   - nMinX = pProgressBarData[3] (offset 0xC)
   - nMinY = pProgressBarData[4] (offset 0x10)
   - nMaxY = nMinY + pProgressBarData[6] (offset 0x18 = height)
6. Calculate nMaxX using FPU value (progress percentage * width)
7. Call GfxValidateClipCoordinates to draw clipped rectangle
8. Return 1 (rendered successfully)

Parameters:
- pProgressBarData (int * in ECX): Pointer to 0x44-byte progress bar structure
  Offset 0x00: eType (must be 10 for D2WIN_PROGRESSBAR)
  Offset 0x08: dwFlags (visibility bit flags)
  Offset 0x0C: nMinX (left coordinate)
  Offset 0x10: nMinY (top coordinate)
  Offset 0x14: nWidth (bar width)
  Offset 0x18: nHeight (bar height)
  Offset 0x40: flProgress (float, current progress 0.0-1.0)

Returns:
- 1: Progress bar was rendered
- 0: Progress bar not visible (flags not set)

Special Cases:
- Assert failure if eType != 10 (not a progress bar)
- Returns 0 without rendering if visibility flags not set

Caller Context:
- Stored at offset 0x1C in progress bar object by AllocateAndInitializeObject
- Called as render callback during UI draw cycle

2. Assert/fatal error if type mismatch
3. Set handler function pointer at offset 0x20

2. Check if message is not WM_KEYDOWN (0x102) AND event type is 0x20 (KEY_DOWN)
3. If conditions pass, retrieve callback pointer from timer vtable offset 0xd
4. If callback exists (non-null), invoke callback with timer data
5. Return 1 if callback was invoked, 0 otherwise

Parameters:

  - [1]: Message type (0x102 = WM_KEYDOWN excluded)
  - [2]: Event flags (0x20 = KEY_DOWN event)

- 0: Conditions not met (wrong message type or no callback)

- Callback at vtable offset 0xd was stored from nCallback in CreateObjectInstance

- Input 1 returns 1 (bit 0 is set)

0x10014A31.name: ProcessCleanupAndExit
0x10014A31.signature: void ProcessCleanupAndExit(uint dwExitCode, int nQuickExit, int nTerminateFlag)
0x10014A31.comment:
Handles DLL/process cleanup operations with selective termination modes.

Algorithm:
1. Call setup function FUN_6ff2b372() to initialize cleanup state
2. Check global termination flag g_dwTerminationActiveFlag - if set to 1, terminate immediately with TerminateProcess
3. Set global cleanup flag g_dwCleanupFlag = 1 to signal cleanup is active  
4. Store terminate flag as byte in g_bTerminateFlagStore for later reference
5. If nQuickExit == 0 (full cleanup mode):
   - Process dynamic function pointer buffer from g_pbDynamicBufferEnd to g_pbDynamicBufferStart
   - Call each non-null function pointer in reverse order (typical destructor pattern)
   - Call static cleanup function pointer arrays from g_ppStaticCleanupArrayStart to g_ppStaticCleanupArrayEnd
6. Always call final cleanup function pointer arrays from g_ppFinalCleanupArrayStart to g_ppFinalCleanupArrayEnd
7. If nTerminateFlag == 0: set g_dwTerminationActiveFlag = 1 and call ExitProcess (no return)
8. Otherwise: call FUN_6ff2b37b() final cleanup and return to caller

Parameters:
dwExitCode (uint): Exit code passed to ExitProcess/TerminateProcess (0-255)
nQuickExit (int): Cleanup mode flag - 0 = full cleanup with dynamic destructors, non-zero = skip dynamic cleanup
nTerminateFlag (int): Termination mode - 0 = ExitProcess (no return), non-zero = return to caller

Returns:
void: No return value when nTerminateFlag == 0 (calls ExitProcess)
      Returns normally when nTerminateFlag != 0 after cleanup

Special Cases:
- If g_dwTerminationActiveFlag already set to 1: bypasses all cleanup, calls TerminateProcess immediately
- If g_pbDynamicBufferStart is null: skips dynamic buffer processing safely
- If dynamic buffer traversal reaches invalid range: stops gracefully at g_pbDynamicBufferStart boundary
- Function pointer arrays are called via CallFunctionPointerArray which handles null ranges safely

Magic Numbers:
0x1 - Cleanup active flag value stored in g_dwCleanupFlag and g_dwTerminationActiveFlag
0x4 - Pointer size decrement for buffer traversal (32-bit function pointers)

Error Handling:
- Uses TerminateProcess for immediate shutdown when termination flag pre-set
- Uses ExitProcess for normal process termination after cleanup
- Function pointer null checks prevent crashes during dynamic cleanup traversal
- Buffer boundary checks prevent memory access violations during traversal

0x10014AE8.name: RunConstructorArray
0x10014AE8.comment:
Executes an array of constructor or initialization function pointers in sequence.

Algorithm:
1. Iterate through function pointer array from ppfnStart to ppfnEnd (exclusive)
2. For each 4-byte aligned function pointer entry:
   a. Load the function pointer value into EAX
   b. Test if pointer is non-null (TEST EAX,EAX) 
   c. Skip null pointers (JZ to increment)
   d. Call the function pointer (CALL EAX) with no parameters
3. Advance to next function pointer (ADD ESI,0x4)
4. Continue until reaching end pointer (CMP ESI,[ESP+0xc])
5. Return when all valid function pointers have been executed

Parameters:
- ppfnStart (void * *): Pointer to start of function pointer array
- ppfnEnd (void * *): Pointer to end of function pointer array (exclusive)

Returns:
- void: No return value

Special Cases:
- Null function pointers are safely skipped without error
- Empty array (ppfnStart == ppfnEnd) exits immediately
- No parameter validation - assumes valid array bounds

Error Handling:
- No explicit error handling
- Relies on caller to provide valid array bounds
- Function calls are made with no error checking

0x10014B10.name: AllocateStackSpace
0x10014B10.comment:
Dynamically allocates stack space with page probing to ensure proper memory commitment.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack pointer to current position plus 8 bytes (beyond return address and saved ECX)
2. Check if requested allocation size exceeds one page (0x1000 bytes)
3. If multi-page allocation needed, enter probing loop:
   - Subtract one page (0x1000 bytes) from stack pointer
   - Subtract one page from remaining allocation size
   - Touch memory at stack pointer to trigger page commitment
   - Repeat until remaining size is less than one page
4. Subtract final remaining bytes from stack pointer
5. Touch memory at final stack position to commit last page
6. Update ESP register to new stack pointer position
7. Restore original ECX and return address from saved stack frame
8. Return to caller with stack space allocated and committed

Parameters:
dwStackSize (uint) - Number of bytes to allocate on stack

Returns:
void - No return value, modifies stack pointer directly

Special Cases:
- Single page allocations (≤ 0xFFF bytes) skip the probing loop
- Memory touches use TEST instruction to trigger page faults for uncommitted pages
- Stack grows downward, so allocation decreases stack pointer
- Function preserves ECX register across call

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1000 (4096) - Windows page size for stack probing
0xFFF (4095) - Maximum single-page allocation without probing

Error Handling:
- No explicit error handling - relies on Windows page fault mechanism
- Invalid memory access triggers system page fault handler
- Stack overflow protection handled by system guard pages

0x10014C40.name: OptimizedMemoryMove
0x10014C40.signature: void * OptimizedMemoryMove(void * pDestination, void * pSource, uint dwByteCount)
0x10014C40.comment:
Optimized memory move implementation with overlap detection and alignment optimization.

Algorithm:
1. Check for overlapping memory regions (source and destination ranges overlap)
2. If overlapping regions detected, copy backwards from end to start to avoid corruption
3. If no overlap, copy forwards from start to end for better cache performance
4. For both directions, optimize copying using 4-byte aligned transfers when possible
5. Handle misaligned data by copying individual bytes first to reach alignment
6. Perform bulk 4-byte transfers in optimized loop (unroll threshold of 8 iterations)
7. Copy remaining bytes (0-3) using individual byte transfers

Parameters:
pDestination - Destination memory buffer to copy data to
pSource - Source memory buffer to copy data from  
dwByteCount - Number of bytes to copy between buffers

Returns:
void * - Returns original destination pointer (pDestination) for function chaining

Special Cases:
Zero byte count - Returns immediately without any memory operations
Misaligned pointers - Falls back to byte-by-byte copying with alignment handling
Large transfers - Uses optimized 4-byte transfers with loop unrolling for performance

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x4 (4) - Alignment boundary and 4-byte transfer size
0x3 (3) - Alignment mask to check 4-byte boundary alignment  
0x7 (7) - Loop unrolling threshold for optimized bulk transfer

Error Handling:
No explicit error checking - assumes valid memory regions and non-null pointers
Overlap detection prevents memory corruption during overlapping copies
Alignment optimization ensures optimal performance on x86 architecture

0x10014F75.name: UpdateSystemTimeCache
0x10014F75.comment:
Updates cached system time values and returns timestamp with timezone adjustment

Algorithm:
1. Get current local time using GetLocalTime into localTime structure
2. Get current system time using GetSystemTime into systemTime structure  
3. Check if current system time matches previously cached values (minute, hour, day, month, year)
4. If time matches cache, skip timezone update and jump to timestamp calculation
5. Call GetTimeZoneInformation to determine current timezone status
6. Set timezone bias based on result: -1 for error, 1 for daylight time, 0 for standard time
7. Update all cached time values with current system time components
8. Call FUN_6ff2d956 with local time components and timezone bias to compute timestamp
9. Store computed timestamp in output parameter if provided

Parameters:
pTimestampOut: Output parameter to receive computed timestamp value, may be NULL

Returns:
void (result returned through output parameter)

Special Cases:
- If GetTimeZoneInformation fails (returns 0xffffffff), timezone bias set to -1
- If timezone is daylight time with valid date and bias, timezone bias set to 1
- If output parameter is NULL, timestamp is computed but not stored
- Time cache comparison optimizes timezone processing when time unchanged

Magic Numbers:
0xffffffff - TIME_ZONE_ID_INVALID from GetTimeZoneInformation
0x2 - TIME_ZONE_ID_DAYLIGHT indicating daylight saving time
1 - Daylight time bias flag
0 - Standard time bias flag
-1 - Timezone error flag

Structure Layout:
_SYSTEMTIME (16 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field        | Type   | Description
0x00   | 2    | wYear        | ushort | Year (1601-30827)
0x02   | 2    | wMonth       | ushort | Month (1-12)
0x04   | 2    | wDayOfWeek   | ushort | Day of week (0-6)
0x06   | 2    | wDay         | ushort | Day of month (1-31)
0x08   | 2    | wHour        | ushort | Hour (0-23)
0x0A   | 2    | wMinute      | ushort | Minute (0-59)
0x0C   | 2    | wSecond      | ushort | Second (0-59)
0x0E   | 2    | wMilliseconds| ushort | Milliseconds (0-999)

g_dwCachedYearMonth: Cached year (low word) and month (high word)
g_dwCachedDayOfWeekDay: Cached day of week (low word) and day (high word)  
g_dwCachedHourMinute: Cached hour (low word) and minute (high word)
g_dwCachedSecondMillisecond: Cached second (low word) and millisecond (high word)

0x10015242.name: IsBindingStateFlagSet
0x10015242.comment:
Check if binding state flag (0x8) is set

1. Compare g_dwBindingMode with 1
2. If g_dwBindingMode > 1: Call FUN_6fb9f44c(pThis, nBindingIndex, 8) and return result

0x100153D3.name: DllMain
0x100153D3.comment:
DLL entry point that handles process and thread attach/detach notifications.

Algorithm:
1. Check dwReason parameter to determine DLL notification type
2. DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH (1): Initialize DLL when process loads
   a. Call GetVersion() to get Windows version and store in global
   b. Extract version components: major (low byte), minor (second byte), build (high word)
   c. Store version data in separate globals for compatibility checks
   d. Call initialization routine to verify DLL can load
   e. Get command line with GetCommandLineA() for argument parsing
   f. Initialize core subsystems in sequence
   g. Increment process reference counter
3. DLL_PROCESS_DETACH (0): Cleanup when process unloads
   a. Check if process reference counter is positive
   b. Decrement process reference counter
   c. Check cleanup flag and call cleanup routine if needed
   d. Shutdown subsystems in reverse order
4. DLL_THREAD_DETACH (3): Handle thread cleanup
   a. Call thread-specific cleanup routine with NULL parameter
5. Return appropriate status code

Parameters:
phinstDLL (void *): HINSTANCE handle to DLL instance (Windows opaque handle type)
  IMPLICIT: Parameter passed but not used in this implementation
dwReason (uint): Reason for calling DLL entry point
  - 1 (DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH): Process is loading DLL
  - 0 (DLL_PROCESS_DETACH): Process is unloading DLL  
  - 3 (DLL_THREAD_DETACH): Thread is exiting

Returns:
bool: Success status
  - true (1): DLL initialization/cleanup succeeded
  - false (0): DLL initialization failed, prevent DLL loading

Special Cases:
- DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH: Returns false if version check or initialization fails
- DLL_PROCESS_DETACH: Only performs cleanup if reference counter > 0
- DLL_THREAD_ATTACH (2): Not handled, falls through to return true
- Invalid dwReason values: Fall through to return true

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1 - DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH constant
0x0 - DLL_PROCESS_DETACH constant  
0x3 - DLL_THREAD_DETACH constant
0xff - Byte mask for extracting version components
0x8 - Bit shift for extracting minor version (second byte)
0x10 - Bit shift for extracting build number (high word)
0x100 - Multiplier for combining major and minor version

Error Handling:
- Version API failure: Continues with uninitialized version globals
- Initialization failure: Returns false to prevent DLL loading
- Cleanup errors: No error propagation, always returns true for detach

Type Design Notes:
- HINSTANCE parameter correctly typed as void* (Windows opaque handle convention)
- SSA temporaries (fResult, nTempResult) used for intermediate calculations

0x100154AC.name: entry
0x100154AC.signature: int entry(HMODULE hModule, int dwReason, void * lpvReserved)
0x100154AC.comment:
DLL entry point that manages module initialization, validation, and cleanup operations.

Algorithm:
1. Save original reason parameter for callback restoration
2. Initialize result with global state from DAT_1003c8b0
3. Handle process/thread attach (reason 1 or 2): call optional callback if available, then initialize module
4. Validate Bink installation location for all entry reasons
5. Handle process detach (reason 1): cleanup on validation failure, perform normal cleanup on success
6. Handle process attach (reason 0) or thread detach (reason 3): perform additional cleanup operations
7. Execute final callback if available and operation successful
8. Return operation result or zero on failure

Parameters:
  HMODULE hModule - Handle to the DLL module being loaded or unloaded
  int dwReason - Reason for calling entry point (0=process attach, 1=process detach, 2=thread attach, 3=thread detach)
  void* lpvReserved - Reserved parameter typically NULL for dynamic loads, non-NULL for static loads

Returns:
  int - Non-zero value indicates successful initialization/cleanup
        Zero indicates failure (prevents DLL loading on attach, ignored on detach)

Special Cases:
  - Callback function pointer at DAT_1003ce14 is optional and may be NULL
  - Global state DAT_1003c8b0 affects initialization flow
  - Process detach (reason 1) has special cleanup behavior on validation failure

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x0 - Process attach reason / NULL callback indicator
  0x1 - Process detach reason
  0x2 - Thread attach reason  
  0x3 - Thread detach reason

Error Handling:
  - Returns 0 immediately if callback returns 0 during attach operations
  - Returns 0 if module initialization fails during attach
  - Cleanup operations continue even if validation fails during detach

0x10015549.name: AmsgExit
0x10015549.comment:
Exit the application with optional console message display.

Algorithm:
1. Check if console display is enabled by testing DAT_1003c8bc == 1
2. If not enabled, check secondary condition: DAT_1003c8bc == 0 AND DAT_1003c8c0 == 1
3. If either condition true, call FUN_1001f7e7() to display console message
4. Call FUN_1001f820(nExitCode) to perform cleanup operations with provided exit code
5. Call exit function through function pointer PTR___exit_1002e48c with code 0xff
6. Function does not return (terminates process)

Parameters:
nExitCode (int): Exit code to pass to cleanup function FUN_1001f820

Returns:
void - Function does not return (terminates process execution)

Special Cases:
- Always calls exit with hardcoded 0xff regardless of input exit code
- Console message display depends on two global flag variables
- Function pointer call suggests dynamic linking or runtime binding

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1 - Console display enabled flag value
0x0 - Console display disabled flag value  
0xff - Hardcoded exit code passed to exit function (255 decimal)

0x10015580.name: FindLastCharacterOccurrence
0x10015580.comment:
Finds the last occurrence of a character in a string using backward search optimization.

Algorithm:
1. Find the end of the string by scanning forward for null terminator using REPNE SCASB
2. Calculate string length by negating and adjusting the counter from step 1
3. Set direction flag (STD) for backward scanning from end of string
4. Search backward for target character using REPNE SCASB with decremented counter
5. Check if character at current position matches target character
6. Return pointer to character if found, otherwise return NULL

Parameters:
lpszString (char *): Null-terminated string to search in
nCharacter (int): Character to find (passed as int but used as char)

Returns:
char *: Pointer to last occurrence of character in string
NULL (0x0): Character not found in string

Special Cases:
Search character 0x00 (null terminator): Returns pointer to string terminator
Empty string input: Returns NULL immediately
Character not present: Returns NULL after full backward scan

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xffffffff: Initial counter value for REPNE SCASB (scan unlimited)
0x0: NULL return value when character not found

0x100155A7.name: InitializeCriticalSections
0x100155A7.comment:
Initialize four critical sections for thread synchronization.

Algorithm:
1. Load InitializeCriticalSection function pointer into ESI register for optimization
2. Initialize first critical section (g_pCriticalSection1) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
3. Initialize second critical section (g_pCriticalSection2) by calling InitializeCriticalSection  
4. Initialize third critical section (g_pCriticalSection3) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
5. Initialize fourth critical section (g_pCriticalSection4) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
6. Restore ESI register and return

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
Function uses register optimization by loading InitializeCriticalSection function pointer 
once into ESI and calling through the register four times instead of direct calls.

Global Variables Referenced:
g_pCriticalSection1 (0x6ff3650c) - Points to first critical section structure
g_pCriticalSection2 (0x6ff364fc) - Points to second critical section structure  
g_pCriticalSection3 (0x6ff364ec) - Points to third critical section structure
g_pCriticalSection4 (0x6ff364cc) - Points to fourth critical section structure

Calling Context:
Called during thread local storage initialization as part of multithreading setup.

0x100155D0.name: CleanupCriticalSections
0x100155D0.comment:
Cleanup and destroy all thread synchronization critical sections.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize pointer to start of critical section array (0x6ff364c8)
2. Loop through array of critical section pointers until end (0x6ff36588)
3. For each entry, check if pointer is non-null
4. Skip predefined special critical sections (PTR_DAT_6ff3650c, PTR_DAT_6ff364fc, PTR_DAT_6ff364ec, PTR_DAT_6ff364cc)
5. If not special section, delete critical section and call cleanup function FUN_6ff2cac5
6. Advance to next array entry (increment by 4 bytes)
7. After main loop, explicitly cleanup the four special critical sections
8. Return to caller

Parameters:
None - function operates on global critical section array

Returns:
void - no return value, cleanup function

Special Cases:
- Four special critical sections skipped in main loop but cleaned up explicitly at end
- Array spans 0x320 bytes (200 pointer entries) from 0x6ff364c8 to 0x6ff36588
- DeleteCriticalSection function pointer loaded from [0x6ff330d8]

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6ff364c8 - Start address of critical section pointer array
0x6ff36588 - End address of critical section pointer array  
0x6ff3650c - Special critical section 1 (PTR_DAT_6ff3650c)
0x6ff364fc - Special critical section 2 (PTR_DAT_6ff364fc)
0x6ff364ec - Special critical section 3 (PTR_DAT_6ff364ec)
0x6ff364cc - Special critical section 4 (PTR_DAT_6ff364cc)
0x6ff330d8 - Function pointer to DeleteCriticalSection
0x4 - Pointer size increment for array iteration

Error Handling:
None - assumes all pointers valid, DeleteCriticalSection handles invalid input

0x1001563C.name: AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex
0x1001563C.comment:
Thread-safe lazy initialization and acquisition of critical section by array index

Algorithm:
1. Calculate pointer to critical section slot in global array g_ppCriticalSections
2. Check if critical section at index is already initialized (non-null)
3. If uninitialized, allocate 0x18 bytes for CRITICAL_SECTION structure
4. If allocation fails, call AmsgExit(0x11) to terminate process
5. Acquire global initialization lock via recursive call AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex(0x11)
6. Double-check critical section is still null (race condition protection)
7. If still null, initialize critical section with InitializeCriticalSection
8. Store initialized critical section pointer in global array
9. If another thread initialized it first, free duplicate allocation with DeallocateMemory
10. Release global initialization lock via FUN_6ff2c45f(0x11)
11. Enter the requested critical section with EnterCriticalSection

Parameters:
nCriticalSectionIndex - Index into global critical section array g_ppCriticalSections
IMPLICIT: Uses global initialization lock at index 0x11 for thread-safe lazy initialization

Returns:
void - Function does not return a value, critical section is held upon return

Special Cases:
Lock index 0x11 (17) is reserved for the global initialization synchronization lock
Process terminates with AmsgExit(0x11) if critical section allocation fails
Double-checked locking pattern prevents race conditions during initialization

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x18 (24 decimal) - Size of Windows CRITICAL_SECTION structure in bytes
0x11 (17 decimal) - Reserved index for global initialization lock

0x1001569D.name: ReleaseCriticalSectionByIndex
0x1001569D.comment:
Releases a CRT critical section lock by its index.

Classification: Leaf function - wrapper around Win32 LeaveCriticalSection.

Algorithm:
1. Index into g_apCrtLocks array using dwLockIndex
2. Call LeaveCriticalSection on the retrieved CRITICAL_SECTION pointer

Parameters:
  dwLockIndex (uint) - Zero-based index into g_apCrtLocks array

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - No bounds checking on index; caller must ensure valid range
  - Must be paired with prior CRT_EnterCritSectByIndex call

Global Data:
  g_apCrtLocks (0x6fc38644) - Array of LPCRITICAL_SECTION pointers

Called By: 12 functions including CRT_EnterCritSectByIndex, CRT_LeaveCritSectExit

0x100156CA.name: ConvertDateTimeToTimestamp
0x100156CA.signature: int ConvertDateTimeToTimestamp(int nYear, int nMonth, int nDay, int nHour, int nMinute, int nSecond, int nDaylightSavingFlag)
0x100156CA.comment:
Converts date and time components to a Unix-style timestamp value.

Algorithm:
1. Validate year is in supported range (1900-1994, offset from 0x76c base)
2. Return -1 if year is outside valid range [0x46, 0x8a] from base
3. Calculate cumulative days from month table at g_adDaysInMonths[nMonth]
4. Add specified day to cumulative month days
5. Apply leap year adjustment: if year divisible by 4 and month > 2, add 1 day
6. Call FUN_6ff306b5() to update internal state
7. Calculate total timestamp: ((nHour + (yearOffset * 365 + daysFromMonth + (year-1)/4) * 24) * 60 + nMinute) * 60 + baseOffset + second
8. Apply timezone adjustment if nDaylightSavingFlag == 1 or timezone check passes
9. Return final timestamp value

Parameters:
nYear - Year value (1900-1994 supported range)
nMonth - Month index (0-11, used to index days table)
nDay - Day of month (1-31)
nHour - Hour component (0-23)
nMinute - Minute component (0-59) 
nSecond - Second component (0-59)
nDaylightSavingFlag - DST flag: 1=apply DST, -1=check timezone, 0=standard time

Returns:
Calculated timestamp as signed integer
-1 if year is outside supported range

Special Cases:
Leap year handling: Years divisible by 4 get +1 day if month > February
Timezone adjustment: Applied based on g_dwTimezoneFlag and DST settings
Base offset: 0x7c558180 provides epoch adjustment

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x76c (1900) - Base year offset for calculations
0x46 (70) - Minimum year offset (1970)
0x8a (138) - Maximum year offset (2038)
0x16d (365) - Days per year for calculation
0x18 (24) - Hours per day
0x3c (60) - Minutes per hour, seconds per minute
0x7c558180 - Unix epoch base offset

Global Data Access:
g_adDaysInMonths[0x6ff38f24] - Table of cumulative days per month
g_dwTimezoneOffset[0x6ff38e40] - Timezone offset value
g_dwTimezoneFlag[0x6ff38e44] - Timezone enabled flag
g_dwDaylightAdjust[0x6ff38e48] - Daylight savings time adjustment

0x1001578C.name: StreamPutChar
0x1001578C.comment:
Writes a single character to a stream with buffering and error handling support.

Algorithm:
1. Validate stream flags - check for invalid flag combinations (0x82 clear OR 0x40 set)
2. Handle buffering reset - if 0x01 flag set, reset position and optionally restore buffer base
3. Setup output mode - clear position, set backup pointer, configure output flags (clear 0x10, set 0x02)
4. Validate special streams - check if stream matches standard descriptors and validate with FUN_6ff3037c
5. Perform stream cleanup - call FUN_6ff30338 if validation passes
6. Choose output path - buffered (flags & 0x108 != 0) or unbuffered output
7. Buffered output - calculate available space, write directly to buffer or call write function
8. Handle buffer exhaustion - get stream descriptor from table and check error flags
9. Error handling - call FUN_6ff30070 if error flag 0x20 is set
10. Unbuffered output - call FUN_6ff30148 with character address and size 1
11. Verify write result - compare returned bytes with expected count
12. Set error state - set flag 0x20 on write failure, return character on success

Parameters:
nCharacter: Character to write (only low 8 bits used)
pStream: Pointer to stream descriptor structure

Returns:
Character value (0x00-0xFF) on successful write
0xFFFFFFFF on error or invalid stream state

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x01: Buffer reset flag
0x02: Output mode flag  
0x10: Buffer restore flag
0x20: Error state flag
0x40: Read-only flag
0x82: Combined invalid flags
0x108: Buffering mode flags
0x24: Stream descriptor stride (36 bytes)
0xFF: Character mask for return value
0xFFFFFFFF: Error return value

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type      Description
0x00    4     pBase         void*     Base buffer pointer
0x04    4     nPosition     int       Current position offset  
0x08    4     pCurrent      void*     Current buffer pointer
0x0C    4     dwFlags       dword     Primary stream flags
0x10    4     dwFlags2      dword     Stream identifier/handle
0x14    4     reserved      dword     Reserved field
0x18    4     nAvailable    int       Available buffer space
0x1C    4     reserved2     dword     Reserved field  
0x20    4     reserved3     dword     Reserved field

Error Handling:
Invalid flags (0x82 clear OR 0x40 set): Set error flag 0x20 and return 0xFFFFFFFF
Buffer exhaustion with error flag: Call error handler FUN_6ff30070
Write operation failure: Set flag 0x20 and return 0xFFFFFFFF  
Standard stream validation failure: Proceed with cleanup and normal flow

0x100158A4.name: FormatStringProcessor
0x100158A4.signature: int FormatStringProcessor(int * pOutputHandler, byte * pbFormatString, uint * ppnArgsPtr)
0x100158A4.comment:
FormatStringProcessor - processes printf-style format strings with variable arguments

Algorithm:
1. Initialize state variables: dwFlags=0, nStateIndex=0, nCharCount=0
2. Begin character-by-character processing loop of format string
3. For each character, determine processing state using lookup table at 0x6ff333e0
4. Execute state machine transitions based on current state (0-7):
   - State 0: Output literal characters, handle character attributes
   - State 1: Initialize format specifier parsing, reset all flags
   - State 2: Parse format flags: space(0x02), hash(0x80), plus(0x01), minus(0x04), zero(0x08)
   - State 3: Parse field width (decimal digits or asterisk for va_arg)
   - State 4: Encountered decimal point, prepare for precision parsing
   - State 5: Parse precision (decimal digits or asterisk for va_arg)  
   - State 6: Parse length modifiers: I64(0x8000), h(0x20), l(0x10), w(0x800)
   - State 7: Process conversion specifiers and generate output
5. For conversion specifiers: handle integer(d,i,u,o,x,X), float(e,E,f,g,G), character(c,C), string(s,S), pointer(p), written count(n)
6. Apply formatting: field width padding, precision truncation, sign prefixes, case conversion
7. Convert wide characters to multibyte when needed using FUN_6ff30505
8. Output formatted result through pOutputHandler callback
9. Continue until null terminator reached
10. Return total character count

Parameters:
  pOutputHandler (int *) - callback function pointer for character output
  pbFormatString (byte *) - printf-style format string to process
  ppnArgsPtr (uint *) - pointer to variable arguments list array

Returns:
  int - total number of characters processed and output, or negative on error

Special Cases:
  - Field width of -1 indicates unlimited width (0x7fffffff)
  - Precision of -1 disables precision limiting
  - Zero flag (0x08) is ignored when left-align flag (0x04) is set
  - Hash flag (0x80) adds prefixes: "0" for octal, "0x"/"0X" for hex
  - I64 modifier (0x8000) enables 64-bit integer processing

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x6ff333e0 - character classification table for format parsing
  0x6ff33400 - state transition table (8 bytes per character class)  
  0x20/0x78 - valid format character range (space to 'x')
  0x7fffffff - unlimited field width sentinel value
  0x30 - ASCII '0', base for digit conversion
  0x39 - ASCII '9', upper limit for digit checking
  0x2a - ASCII '*', indicates va_arg width/precision
  0x2d - ASCII '-', negative sign character

Error Handling:
  - Invalid format characters fall through to literal output
  - Null string arguments replaced with default "(null)" string
  - Negative field widths converted to left-align with positive width
  - Buffer overflow protection through character count tracking

0x10015FE5.name: BufferedPutChar
0x10015FE5.signature: int BufferedPutChar(byte bCharacter, FileBuffer * pBuffer, int * pnCharsWritten)
0x10015FE5.comment:
Writes a single character to a buffered output stream with automatic flushing.

Algorithm:
1. Decrement the buffer's remaining byte count
2. If buffer has space (count >= 0):
   a. Store character at current buffer position
   b. Increment buffer pointer
   c. Return character value (masked to 8 bits)
3. If buffer is full (count < 0):
   a. Call flush/refill function FUN_6ff2d034
   b. Use its return value as result
4. Check for error condition (-1 return value):
   a. If error: set chars written counter to -1
   b. If success: increment chars written counter

Parameters:
chCharacter (byte) - Character to write to buffer (0-255)
pBuffer (FileBuffer *) - Pointer to buffer structure containing:
  - pbCurrent: Current write position in buffer
  - dwBytesRemaining: Number of bytes left in buffer
pnCharsWritten (int *) - Pointer to character count/status tracker

Returns:
Character value (0-255) on success
-1 (0xFFFFFFFF) on error or buffer flush failure

Special Cases:
If buffer flush operation fails, error state is propagated to caller
Characters are masked to 8 bits (param_1 & 0xff) for return value
Negative buffer count triggers automatic flush/refill operation

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Error indicator for failed operations

Structure Layout:
FileBuffer (8 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name         Type    Description
0x00    4     pbCurrent          byte*   Current write position
0x04    4     dwBytesRemaining   uint    Bytes remaining in buffer

0x1001601A.name: RepeatCharacterToStream
0x1001601A.signature: void RepeatCharacterToStream(uint dwCharacter, int nCount, int * pOutputStream, int * pnErrorStatus)
0x1001601A.comment:
Writes a specified character to an output stream a given number of times.

Algorithm:
1. Check if repeat count is positive, return immediately if zero or negative
2. Enter loop to repeat character output nCount times
3. Call FUN_6ff2d88d to write dwCharacter to pOutputStream 
4. Check error status after each write operation
5. If *pnErrorStatus equals -1, terminate early with error
6. Decrement count and continue loop if count > 0
7. Exit when all characters written or error encountered

Parameters:
dwCharacter (uint): Character code to repeat (typically ASCII value 0x20 for space, 0x30 for '0')
nCount (int): Number of times to repeat the character 
pOutputStream (int *): Pointer to output stream buffer structure
pnErrorStatus (int *): Pointer to error status flag, set to -1 on write failure

Returns:
void: No return value, error status communicated through pnErrorStatus

Special Cases:
- If nCount <= 0, function returns immediately without writing
- Loop terminates early if write operation sets *pnErrorStatus to -1
- Used for padding in printf formatting (spaces, zeros)

Error Handling:
- Monitors error status after each character write
- Early termination on first write failure (-1 status)
- Calling function must check pnErrorStatus for final status

0x1001604B.name: WriteStringToBuffer
0x1001604B.signature: void WriteStringToBuffer(char * lpszString, int nLength, FileBuffer * pBuffer, int * pnCharsWritten)
0x1001604B.comment:
Writes a string to a buffered output stream character by character with error checking.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that string length is greater than zero
2. Initialize loop variables and counters  
3. For each character in the string:
   a. Decrement remaining character count
   b. Load current character from string pointer
   c. Advance string pointer to next character
   d. Call BufferedPutChar to write character to buffer
   e. Check if write operation failed (error code -1)
   f. If error occurred, exit immediately
   g. If characters remain, continue to next character
4. Return when all characters processed or error encountered

Parameters:
lpszString (char *): Pointer to null-terminated or fixed-length string to write
nLength (int): Number of characters to write from string
pBuffer (FileBuffer *): Pointer to buffered output stream structure
pnCharsWritten (int *): Pointer to counter tracking total characters written

Returns:
void - No return value; error status communicated through pnCharsWritten pointer

Special Cases:
If nLength <= 0, function returns immediately without processing
If BufferedPutChar fails (sets *pnCharsWritten to -1), loop exits early
String pointer is advanced byte-by-byte regardless of character encoding

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1: Byte increment for string pointer advancement (0x6ff2d90d: INC ESI)
-1 (0xFFFFFFFF): Error status code indicating write failure (0x6ff2d91b: CMP dword ptr [EDI],-0x1)

0x10016083.name: ReadAndAdvancePointer
0x10016083.comment:
Reads a 32-bit value from current pointer position and advances the pointer by one element.

Algorithm:
1. Read current value from the pointed-to pointer location
2. Advance the pointed-to pointer by 4 bytes (one uint element)
3. Return the value that was at the original position before advancement

Parameters:
ppuCursor - Pointer to pointer tracking current read position in data stream

Returns:
The 32-bit unsigned integer value that was at the current position before advancement

Special Cases:
This function implements a common "read and advance" pattern used in serialization 
and parsing operations. The caller maintains a cursor pointer that gets automatically
advanced after each read operation.

0x10016090.name: ReadLongLongAndAdvancePointer
0x10016090.comment:
ReadLongLongAndAdvancePointer - reads 8-byte value from variable arguments pointer and advances pointer

Algorithm:
1. Dereference pointer to get current position in arguments array
2. Advance the pointer by 8 bytes (2 * sizeof(uint)) to skip over the 8-byte value
3. Read and return the 8-byte value from the original position before advancement

Parameters:
  ppnArgsPtr (uint **) - pointer to variable arguments array pointer, modified in place

Returns:
  longlong - 8-byte signed integer value read from the arguments array

Special Cases:
  - Used specifically for I64 length modifier in printf format processing
  - Advances pointer by exactly 8 bytes regardless of actual data alignment
  - Reads value from position before advancement (offset -8 from new position)

  0x8 - size in bytes of 64-bit value (2 * sizeof(uint))
  -0x8 - negative offset to read value from position before advancement

0x100160A0.name: ReadShortAndAdvancePointer
0x100160A0.comment:
Reads a 16-bit value from variadic arguments and advances pointer

Algorithm:
1. Advance the arguments pointer by 4 bytes to next argument position
2. Read 16-bit value from previous argument position (offset -4)
3. Combine with high 16 bits of current pointer value
4. Return composite 32-bit value

Parameters:
  ppnArgsPtr (uint **) - pointer to variadic arguments pointer array

Returns:
  uint - composite value with previous 16-bit argument in low bits

Special Cases:
  - Advances pointer before reading value from previous position
  - Combines current high bits with previous low 16 bits using CONCAT22

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x4 - argument stride (4 bytes per 32-bit argument)
  -0x4 - offset to read previous argument position

0x100160AE.name: ConfigureSubsystemParameters
0x100160AE.comment:
Configures subsystem initialization parameters with predefined buffer and flag values.

Algorithm:
1. Call FUN_1001fc6c with context pointer and two configuration constants
2. Pass 0x10000 (65536) as buffer size parameter
3. Pass 0x30000 (196608) as flags/configuration parameter
4. Return immediately after configuration call

Parameters:
pContext - Pointer to InitContext structure containing subsystem state

Returns:
void - No return value, configuration applied through context pointer

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x10000 (65536) - Buffer size parameter, likely initial buffer allocation
0x30000 (196608) - Configuration flags parameter, specifies subsystem options

0x100160C0.name: CheckFloatingPointModulus
0x100160C0.comment:
Checks if the modulus operation result is less than pi constant

Algorithm:
1. Load dividend value from g_dDividend (0x100282c8)
2. Load divisor value from g_dDivisor (0x100282d0)

Function handles two different locale modes based on DAT_1002e914 threshold
Character lookup table uses stride of 2 bytes per character entry

0x100165C2.name: InitializeThreadLocalStorage
0x100165C2.comment:
Initialize thread-local storage for per-thread context management

Algorithm:
1. Call cleanup routine to prepare for TLS initialization
2. Allocate TLS slot using TlsAlloc(), store in global g_dwTlsSlotIndex  
3. Check if TLS allocation succeeded (index != 0xFFFFFFFF)
4. Allocate ThreadContext structure memory (116 bytes) via custom allocator
5. Verify ThreadContext allocation succeeded (pointer not NULL)
6. Associate ThreadContext with TLS slot using TlsSetValue()
7. Verify TLS value was set successfully
8. Initialize ThreadContext structure with InitializeThreadContext()
9. Get current thread ID and store in context structure
10. Set context flags field to 0xFFFFFFFF (all flags enabled)
11. Store thread ID in first field of context structure
12. Return success status

Parameters:
None

Returns:
bool: true (1) on successful TLS initialization, false (0) on any failure

Special Cases:
If TLS allocation fails (returns 0xFFFFFFFF), function exits immediately with failure
If memory allocation fails, function exits with failure  
If TLS value cannot be set, function exits with failure
Each failure condition branches to common exit_failure label

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x74 (116 decimal): Size of ThreadContext structure allocation
0xFFFFFFFF: Invalid TLS index return value indicating allocation failure
0xFFFFFFFF: Flag mask for enabling all context flags

Error Handling:

Memory allocation failure: return 0  
TLS value set failure: return 0
All errors result in immediate function exit with false return value

- Process termination if TLS storage assignment fails

0x1001675A.name: InitializeStdIoStreams
0x1001675A.comment:
Initializes C runtime standard I/O stream descriptors for stdin/stdout/stderr

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x480 bytes for initial StreamIO descriptor block (32 streams)
2. Initialize all 32 stream descriptors with default state (closed, flags 0x0A)
3. Call GetStartupInfoA to retrieve process startup information
4. If startup info contains inherited handles (cbReserved2 != 0):
   a. Parse handle table from lpReserved2 pointer
   b. Limit handle count to 0x800 maximum for memory safety
   c. Allocate additional StreamIO blocks if needed (32 streams per block)
   d. For each inherited handle: validate handle and flags, set stream descriptor
5. For streams 0, 1, 2 (stdin/stdout/stderr): if not inherited, get standard handles
6. Set handle type flags based on GetFileType: 0x08 for pipes, 0x40 for character devices
7. Call SetHandleCount with total allocated handle count

Parameters:
None

Returns:
None (void function)

Special Cases:
- Memory allocation failure triggers AmsgExit(0x1B) - fatal error
- Invalid handles (0xFFFFFFFF) are marked with 0x81 flags  
- Handle count clamped to 0x800 maximum to prevent excessive memory allocation
- Stream indices use bit operations: bucket = index >> 5, offset = index & 0x1F

Magic Numbers:
0x480 = 1152 bytes = 32 * 36 byte StreamIO structures per allocation block
0x20 = 32 streams per descriptor block  
0x24 = 36 bytes = size of StreamIO structure
0x800 = 2048 maximum inherited handles supported
0x1B = 27 decimal = exit code for memory allocation failure
0xFFFFFFF6 = STD_INPUT_HANDLE (-10)
0xFFFFFFF5 = STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE (-11) 
0xFFFFFFF4 = STD_ERROR_HANDLE (-12)
0x81 = stream flags for standard handles (binary mode + allocated)
0x80 = STREAM_ALLOCATED flag
0x40 = STREAM_CHARACTER_DEVICE flag (console)
0x08 = STREAM_PIPE flag
0x01 = inherited handle valid flag in startup info
0x0A = 10 decimal = default stream flags (line buffered)

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
-------|------|------------|------|------------
0x00   | 4    | pBase      | void*| File handle or buffer pointer  
0x04   | 1    | nPosition  | byte | Stream status flags
0x05   | 1    | (padding)  | byte | Line buffer mode (0x0A = LF)
0x08   | 4    | pCurrent   | void*| Current position in buffer
0x0C   | 24   | (other)    | -    | Additional StreamIO fields

Flag Bits:
0x01 = STREAM_VALID (handle inherited and valid)
0x08 = STREAM_PIPE (pipe handle type)  
0x40 = STREAM_CHARACTER (character device - console)
0x80 = STREAM_ALLOCATED (descriptor allocated and active)
0x81 = STREAM_STANDARD (standard handle - stdin/stdout/stderr)

0x10016916.name: CleanupStreamDescriptors
0x10016916.comment:

1. Initialize pointer to global stream descriptor array at 0x6ff3b440
2. For each descriptor pointer in the array (up to 0x6ff3b540):
   a. Check if descriptor pointer is non-null
   b. If valid, iterate through 32 StreamIO structures (0x20 entries)
   c. For each StreamIO structure, check critical section at offset -4 from dwFlags
   d. If critical section exists, call DeleteCriticalSection to cleanup
   e. Advance to next StreamIO structure (0x24 byte stride)
3. After processing all structures in descriptor, deallocate entire descriptor memory
4. Set descriptor pointer to null to prevent double-free
5. Move to next descriptor pointer and repeat

None

Returns:

Special Cases:
- Handles null descriptor pointers safely by skipping
- Uses boundary checking (pStreamEnd < pStreamEnd + 0x20) for validation
- Critical section cleanup only performed if critical section field is non-null
- Memory deallocation performed after all critical sections cleaned up

- 0x24 (36): Size of each StreamIO structure in bytes
- 0x6ff3b440: Base address of global stream descriptor array
- 0x6ff3b540: End address of global stream descriptor array
- -0x4: Offset from dwFlags field to critical section field in StreamIO structure

Offset | Size | Field Name        | Type                    | Description

0x1001696A.name: InitializeEnvironmentVariables
0x1001696A.comment:

0x3D (61) - ASCII value for '=' character used to filter assignments

7. Validate allocation success; exit with code 8 if malloc fails

0x10016ABC.name: ParseCommandLineArguments
0x10016ABC.signature: void ParseCommandLineArguments(char * lpszCmdLine, char * * lpszArgv, char * szOutputBuffer, int * pnArgc, int * pnTotalChars)
0x10016ABC.comment:
Parses command line string into individual arguments with quote and escape handling

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output counters: set argc=1, totalChars=0
2. Store first argument pointer in argv[0] if argv provided
3. Check if command line starts with quote (0x22):
   a. If quoted: Parse until closing quote, handle escape sequences
   b. If unquoted: Parse until space (0x20) or tab (0x09)
4. Use character lookup table at 0x1003cbc0 bit 4 to identify escapable chars
5. Skip whitespace between arguments using space/tab delimiters
6. For each argument found:
   a. Store argument pointer in argv array if provided
   b. Increment argc counter
   c. Handle backslash escape sequences (\\ becomes \)
   d. Toggle quote mode on unescaped quotes, handle doubled quotes ("")
   e. Copy characters to output buffer if provided
   f. Null-terminate argument in output buffer
7. Null-terminate argv array and increment argc for final count

Parameters:
- cmdLine: Input command line string to parse
- argv: Array to store pointers to parsed arguments (NULL = count only)
- outputBuffer: Buffer to store null-terminated argument strings (NULL = count only)
- argc: Pointer to receive argument count (includes program name)
- totalChars: Pointer to receive total characters needed for all arguments

Returns:
- void (results returned through output parameters)

Special Cases:
- If argv is NULL: Only counts arguments without storing pointers
- If outputBuffer is NULL: Only counts characters without copying
- Empty quotes "" create empty argument
- Backslash at end of line becomes literal backslash
- Doubled quotes ("") inside quoted string become single quote

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x22 (34): Double quote character for argument quoting
- 0x20 (32): Space character - argument delimiter
- 0x09 (9): Tab character - argument delimiter  
- 0x5C (92): Backslash character for escape sequences
- 0x1003cbc0: Character classification table base address
- 0x4: Bit mask for escapable character flag in lookup table

Character Classification Table:
The lookup table at 0x1003cbc0 contains character class flags where
bit 4 (value 0x4) indicates characters that require escape handling.
This typically includes characters like quotes, backslashes, and 
other shell metacharacters that need special processing.

0x10016C70.name: GetEnvironmentStringsConverted
0x10016C70.comment:
Retrieves and converts environment strings to ANSI format with automatic Unicode/ANSI detection.

Algorithm:
1. Check global state flag DAT_1003ca4c for preferred string format
2. If state is 0 (uninitialized), attempt Unicode path first via GetEnvironmentStringsW()
3. If Unicode strings available, set state to 1 (Unicode mode) and process wide strings
4. If Unicode fails, fall back to ANSI path via GetEnvironmentStrings() and set state to 2
5. For Unicode processing: iterate through null-terminated string array to calculate total length
6. Convert wide character count to byte count and call WideCharToMultiByte() for size estimation
7. Allocate buffer using malloc() with required size
8. Perform actual conversion using WideCharToMultiByte() to allocated buffer
9. If conversion fails, free buffer and return NULL
10. For ANSI processing: iterate through ANSI string array to calculate total length
11. Allocate buffer and copy strings using FUN_100217e0 (memory copy function)
12. Free original environment strings using appropriate API (W or A version)
13. Return allocated buffer containing converted environment strings

Parameters:
